findings.breaking_input: `arc launch apply payment-live --venture arc-sandbox --provider <any string pickProvider accepts>`, for example a differently cased id or an alias form if pickProvider normalises its match. On a slot with a single vetted row, pickProvider validates the flag, but the gate then receives `opts.provider` (the raw argv string) instead of the row pickProvider chose.
findings.why: This is a validate-one-value, use-another case. The `approval.requested` payload and the `what` line carry the user's spelling, not the registry id. The result of pickProvider is discarded. The owner's stamp and any later provider matching key on a string that is not a row id. It is also unsanitised argv text written to the spine, where the main path writes `prow.id`.
findings.fix: Use the id from pickProvider's return value (`const p = pickProvider(...); providerId = p.id`), and never pass `opts.provider` through to the gate.
findings.twin_of: validate one read, use another: every check-then-load pair

findings.breaking_input: The hash input is a template literal that contains a raw line break (`${ctx.tag}<LF>${payment}`). A Windows checkout with autocrlf, an editor that re-saves the file, or a shell-written edit can turn that break into CRLF or strip it. JS normalises CRLF inside a template literal, but a normaliser that rewrites the break to a space or removes it changes `event` and `refund` for every venture.
findings.why: The probe event id and refund id are the replay identity the route stored. A silent change to the separator makes every re-verify look like a new refund. That is the 'new payment' path, so a stored refund row is orphaned, and the 'launch did not send' check then fails the probe permanently. The separator is invisible in review, and this repo's own rule says a program embedded in shell text must not depend on such characters.
findings.fix: Write the separator as an explicit escape in an ordinary string, for example `ctx.tag + "\u0000" + payment` or `JSON.stringify([ctx.tag, payment])`. Pin the expected id for a fixed tag and payment in a test.
findings.twin_of: Windows CRLF vs LF in checked-out text: every test fixture or literal that edits or depends on checked-out line endings

findings.breaking_input: A `refund.processed` row for the probe payment whose stored body is not valid JSON, or whose `payload.refund.entity` is missing. The CTE filters the rows correctly, but the select list still casts `body::jsonb` for every surviving row, so one such row aborts the whole query.
findings.why: The B1 fix only ensures that rows of other events are not cast. A malformed refund.processed row of the same payment still throws a Postgres error for the entire read. verify then reports an opaque 'error: ...' reason and the slot wedges until someone deletes the row by hand. No coded refusal names the cause.
findings.fix: Parse each body once in the CTE, guarded by `case when pg_input_is_valid(body, 'jsonb') then body::jsonb end`, or compare `body ~ '^\s*\{'`. Report a row with a null refund_id as 'a refund.processed row launch did not send'.
findings.twin_of: The refund read cast every stored body to jsonb in the select list: every SQL cast over a column others write: filter first, cast after
